prompt: What does a standard secondary DNS zone contain?
options: A full read-only authoritative copy of the zone
Only recently cached client responses
Only the addresses of authoritative servers
A writable replica stored through AD replication
en: A secondary holds full zone data read-only, unlike a cache or stub.
ru: Secondary full zone data read-only rakhta hai; cache ya stub se alag hai.

prompt: Where should ordinary record changes be made in a standard primary/secondary design?
options: At the writable primary zone
Directly in every secondary copy
Only in the client hosts file
In the secondary server’s reverse zone regardless of the record
en: The primary is the editing source; the secondary receives replicated changes.
ru: Primary editing source hai; secondary replicated changes leta hai.

prompt: What is a master server in a secondary-zone configuration?
options: A server supplying zone data to that secondary
The client’s required default gateway
The only domain controller permitted in a forest
The first resolver in every client’s DNS list
en: A master is the transfer source and may host a primary or another secondary copy.
ru: Master transfer source hai; primary ya doosri secondary copy host kar sakta hai.

prompt: Which SOA field helps identify a newer zone version?
options: Serial number
Primary DNS suffix
Client subnet mask
CNAME target length
en: The serial is used in checking whether a newer zone version is available.
ru: Serial se check hota hai ke zone ka naya version available hai ya nahin.

prompt: What does a DNS Notify message do?
options: Prompts a recipient to check for zone changes
Contains proof that all new records were transferred
Converts the recipient into a writable primary
Sets the recipient’s default gateway
en: Notify is a change signal, not evidence of a completed transfer.
ru: Notify change ka signal hai, completed transfer ki evidence nahin.

prompt: Which transfer type requests a full zone transfer?
options: AXFR
IXFR
PTR
CNAME
en: AXFR transfers the full zone; IXFR supports incremental changes.
ru: AXFR full zone transfer hai; IXFR incremental changes ke liye hai.

prompt: Which transfer type supports incremental zone updates?
options: IXFR
AXFR
AAAA
MX
en: IXFR can transfer differences; availability and retained change history affect transfer behavior.
ru: IXFR differences transfer kar sakta hai; support aur change history behavior affect karte hain.

prompt: Which transport must be allowed for a standard full AXFR transfer?
options: TCP port 53
UDP port 67
TCP port 3389
UDP port 123
en: Full AXFR uses TCP 53. DNS queries also require appropriate UDP/TCP access.
ru: Full AXFR TCP 53 use karta hai; queries ke liye munasib UDP/TCP access bhi chahiye.

prompt: What does a secondary zone’s SOA expiry interval govern?
options: How long it can serve without a successful refresh before the copy expires
The lifetime of every client-side cached record
The duration of a Windows user password
The interval before automatic conversion to primary
en: Zone expiry limits stale secondary service; record-cache TTL is a different timer.
ru: Zone expiry stale secondary service ki had hai; cache TTL alag timer hai.

prompt: How are forward and reverse secondary zones related?
options: They are separate zone configurations requiring their own data and transfer settings
Creating either one automatically creates the other
They share one zone name and record set
A reverse secondary can store only CNAME records
en: Forward and reverse are separate namespaces and must be configured and verified separately.
ru: Forward aur reverse alag namespaces hain; configuration aur verification alag hoti hai.

prompt: In the classroom lab, DNS02 is .122 and DNS01 is .121. Which master address belongs in DNS02’s secondary wizard?
en: DNS01 is the recorded transfer source for DNS02.
ru: DNS02 ke liye recorded transfer source DNS01 hai.

prompt: Which destination should DNS01 authorize to transfer the zone to DNS02?
options: Only DNS01’s own address, 192.168.0.121
Only the subnet mask 255.255.255.0
Every Internet address without restriction
en: The transfer recipient must be authorized; permitting only the source’s own IP does not authorize DNS02.
ru: Transfer recipient authorized hona chahiye; source ka apna IP allow karna DNS02 ki permission nahin.

prompt: DNS02 must host a secondary for VCPLAB.Com. What zone name should be entered?
options: VCPLAB.Com
DNS02 only
The VMware folder name DNS
en: The secondary copies the same zone namespace hosted by its master.
ru: Secondary master ki usi zone namespace ki copy leta hai.

prompt: Which reverse-zone name matches the classroom 192.168.0.0/24 network?
options: 0.168.192.in-addr.arpa
192.168.0.in-addr.arpa
122.168.192.in-addr.arpa
VCPLAB.Com.reverse
en: The three /24 network octets are reversed under in-addr.arpa.
ru: /24 ke teen network octets ulat kar in-addr.arpa ke saath aate hain.

prompt: DNS02 displays SOA, NS, host A records and the DNS alias after transfer. What is established?
options: Those records loaded into the secondary zone
A primary-outage test has passed
Every future update is guaranteed to arrive
DNS02 has become an AD domain controller
en: Loaded records establish the captured copy state, not outage recovery or future guarantees.
ru: Loaded records captured copy state dikhate hain, outage recovery ya future guarantee nahin.

prompt: Which command directly tests DNS02’s forward DNS service for DNS01’s name?
options: nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.122
nslookup dns02.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup dns03.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.123
en: The final argument selects DNS02; the question asks for DNS01’s record.
ru: Aakhri argument DNS02 choose karta hai; sawal DNS01 ke record ka hai.

prompt: Which command tests DNS01’s reverse mapping through DNS02?
options: nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup -type=CNAME vcplab.com. 192.168.0.122
en: The first IP is the reverse subject; the second is the responding DNS server.
ru: Pehla IP reverse subject aur doosra responding DNS server hai.

prompt: DNS01 is unavailable, but DNS02 is reachable and its zone copy remains valid. What can DNS02 do?
options: Answer existing records from its own copy without promotion
Answer only after becoming a writable primary
Obtain each requested record from the offline primary
Automatically remove all existing records
en: A valid secondary already provides authoritative answers for its zone data.
ru: Valid secondary apni zone data ke authoritative answers pehle hi de sakta hai.

prompt: What is a strong test that a new edit reached DNS02?
options: Add a controlled test record on DNS01 and query that record directly on DNS02
Query an unchanged old record only on DNS01
Observe that DNS01 has a Notify button
Ping the DNS02 machine without a DNS query
en: Testing the known new record on the recipient checks the update rather than only old data or reachability.
ru: Known naya record recipient par test karna update check karta hai, sirf purana data ya reachability nahin.

prompt: DNS03’s IP is included in a classroom transfer list, but DNS03 hosts a stub. What does that permission imply?
options: Permission alone does not turn DNS03 into a full secondary
DNS03 now stores every ordinary record automatically
DNS03 becomes writable because its IP is listed
DNS02’s zone automatically changes to a stub
en: Authorization and the recipient’s zone role are distinct settings.
ru: Authorization aur recipient ka zone role alag settings hain.

prompt: DNS02 receives no zone data after setup. Which checks are most relevant?
options: Exact zone name, master address, transfer authorization, service and network path
Only whether the desktop can open a public website
Only whether DNS02’s display name is uppercase
Only whether the VM folder is named DNS
en: Zone transfer needs matching zone identity, a valid source, permission and connectivity.
ru: Zone transfer ke liye matching zone, valid source, permission aur connectivity chahiye.

prompt: Ordinary DNS queries succeed, but full zone transfer fails. What remains a useful check?
options: TCP 53 connectivity and transfer permissions for DNS02
Assume every DNS operation must work if one query works
Replace all A records with PTR records
Disable the secondary zone to make it writable
en: Query success alone does not prove TCP AXFR access or authorization.
ru: Query success TCP AXFR access ya authorization ka proof nahin.

prompt: DNS02 answers an old value after DNS01 was changed. Which investigation fits?
options: Compare SOA serials and check refresh/transfer state on DNS02
Reinstall Windows before inspecting DNS
Change the client gateway to DNS01’s address immediately
Delete the forward zone because a reverse lookup works
en: The secondary may be stale; compare versions and transfer status before unrelated changes.
ru: Secondary stale ho sakta hai; unrelated changes se pehle versions aur transfer state compare hon.

prompt: Forward queries succeed on DNS02, but reverse queries fail. What should be inspected?
options: The reverse secondary zone, its PTR data and its transfer settings
Only the forward CNAME record
Only the DNS suffix of an unrelated workstation
The primary’s wallpaper and display resolution
en: Forward success does not establish reverse-zone configuration or PTR replication.
ru: Forward success reverse-zone configuration ya PTR replication establish nahin karti.

prompt: An accidental record deletion appears on both primary and secondary. What lesson follows?
options: Replication is not a substitute for recoverable backups
Secondaries cannot receive deletions
A full secondary copy is always an immutable backup
Notify can recreate any deleted record automatically
en: Correct replication can propagate mistakes, so recovery requires appropriate backups and procedures.
ru: Sahi replication ghalti bhi copy kar sakti hai; recovery ke liye backups aur procedures chahiye.
